purpose: Check a confound after inspecting the 14-channel same-device and 3-channel transfer scores. Hold the number and type of predictors fixed. Use R1-R3 (A) and R4-R6 (B), all same manufacturer/type, in the complete four train/test combinations A/A, A/B, B/A, B/B. Same source dates and same later exposure IDs and feedback across all four; all are now retrospective paired development comparisons.
one_decision: Fix two alternatives to the misleading earliest-possible choose-once comparator before scoring. All recipes give identical predictions on batch 1 by construction. (i) Practical once: initially use pooled-source; make exactly one decision after a completed batch in which any of the four fitted candidate recipes actually disagreed on the returned rows. Rank the four based on cumulative pre-label scores at that moment, with the same 0.01 change margin; freeze immediately even on a tie. (ii) Fixed recipe schedule: first two batches pooled-source, all later batches local-source. Include the pre-existing cumulative selector and all four fixed recipes. No future selection of the day on which to decide. Repeated seed grid is already frozen. Apply same revised once and fixed local schedule on official too.
claims: Report seed-17 scores, means on 13 feedback draws, counts of improvements over practical-once; group by A to A versus A to B, and B to B versus B to A. Compute worst-class recall separately. Determine whether gains require continued decisions, whether source omission helps due to replaced hardware or merely fewer channels. No new independent-source claim. Do not select the winning direction for promotion.
